confirmed.title: acquire_lock dead-pid branch keeps the lock-steal race r3 #4 fixed only for the pidless branch
confirmed.claim: The review-r3 #4 fix (never rmtree a lock another starter may have just created) was applied only to the missing/garbled-pid branch (run.py:81-94, age-gated). The dead-pid branch at run.py:77-80 still does an unguarded check-then-rmtree-then-retry-mkdir: `if _pid_is_pipeline(pid): return False; shutil.rmtree(cfg.lock_dir, ...)` with no re-verification that the directory it deletes is still the stale one. Two processes racing through this branch can both acquire the lock and run two full concurrent pipelines against the same ledger, work/, and stage/ trees.
confirmed.evidence: run.py:69-95: the loop retries mkdir after rmtree. Dead-pid path has no age gate and no ownership re-check before rmtree, unlike the sibling branch whose comment states the exact hazard: "rmtree-after-grace could steal a JUST-mkdir'd winner's lock and yield two concurrent runs (review-r3 #4)". test_run.py:16-21 covers only the single-process reclaim, not the race. Once two runs are live nothing else protects the pipeline: each process builds its own private `attempted` set (run.py:819) and D-thread, so both `ingest.next_batch` calls return the same DISCOVERED sessions; state guards are read-then-act across processes (ledger.set_state run.py/ledger.py:115-127 is not compare-and-swap), so both can pass the READY check in _deliver_phase (run.py:487) before either commits PACKAGED.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A run crashes hard (SIGKILL/OOM) leaving run.lock with a dead pid. The systemd tick and a manual `python -m pipeline run` (or two manual runs) start near-simultaneously. Both fail mkdir, both read the dead pid, both see _pid_is_pipeline()==False. Process A is descheduled between the pid check and rmtree; process B rmtrees, mkdirs, and writes its pid; A's rmtree then deletes B's live lock and A's second-pass mkdir succeeds — both processes now hold the lock. Both D threads batch the same DISCOVERED sessions; both fix/cut the same session concurrently (two ffmpeg processes writing the same work/<sid>-pN/video.mp4 can produce a torn segment), and around the UTC-midnight boundary the two processes stage the same session under two different dates (deliver.py:78-79 upload_date_utc), yielding a verified double-delivery at two Drive II paths.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the dead-pid reclaim collision-proof: after rmtree, attempt mkdir in the same iteration and, on success, re-read the pid file after writing it to confirm ownership; or gate the dead-pid rmtree on lock-dir age like the pidless branch; or replace the scheme with an O_EXCL pid-file (os.open(pid, O_CREAT|O_EXCL)) plus atomic rename so reclaim can never delete a freshly created winner's lock.
confirmed.verifier_reasoning: Verified. run.py:76-80: the dead-pid branch does read-pid -> _pid_is_pipeline -> shutil.rmtree with no age gate and no re-verification, inside a retry loop (for _ in range(2)) that re-attempts mkdir after the rmtree; only the ValueError/FileNotFoundError branch (81-94) got the review-r3 #4 guard, whose own comment names the exact hazard. Interleaving traces: A reads dead pid and is descheduled; B reads dead pid, rmtrees, mkdirs, writes its pid; A resumes and rmtrees B's LIVE lock dir, then A's second mkdir succeeds — two holders. Downstream protections are absent as claimed: ledger.set_state (ledger.py:115-127) is a read-then-UPDATE with no state precondition (not CAS), _deliver_phase's READY/PACKAGED/UPLOADED check (run.py:487) is read-then-act, each process has its own private `attempted` set (run.py:822), and next_batch excludes only per-process attempted ids — so both runs claim the same DISCOVERED sessions. The double-delivery variant is real but needs a cross-midnight window (deliver.py:53-79: both processes race staged_date then use their own upload_date_utc); same-date concurrent staging collides on one path. Trigger requires a stale dead-pid lock plus two near-simultaneous starts plus a microsecond-scale deschedule — real (systemd tick + manual run after a SIGKILL) but improbable, and the worst outcomes need further coincidences. MAJOR, matching the reviewer's grade: concurrent-run corruption/torn segments and potential double-delivery, but a narrow, multi-precondition race rather than a routinely-reachable BLOCKER.

confirmed.title: Transient host-level OSError in download() outside _unzip_payload permanently quarantines good sessions (r3 #44 fix incomplete)
confirmed.claim: Review-r3 #44 established that host-level OSErrors (disk full, I/O hiccup) during download must be transient/retryable, but the fix was applied only inside _unzip_payload (ingest.py:471-477). Every other filesystem operation in download() — _md5_file over the multi-GB video (ingest.py:535 and 581), shutil.move of the v2 sidecars (ingest.py:565-567), rrdmod.write_script (ingest.py:570), stub.touch (ingest.py:573), dst.mkdir (ingest.py:520/539) — still raises a raw OSError, which _download_phase's catch-all (run.py:188-197) converts to a terminal QUARANTINED ("download crashed: ..."). Because the checksum-verified download succeeded, the Drive-side bytes and ctime are unchanged, so neither healing path in scan() can ever fire: the path-heal needs a different drive_path (ingest.py:207-230) and the zip/md5 supersedes need changed bytes/ctime/md5 (ingest.py:238-294). The session is lost permanently unless the operator re-uploads modified bytes.
confirmed.evidence: ingest.py:471-477 catches OSError only around zip extraction with the comment "host-level errors are TRANSIENT ... a quarantine here would make a full disk permanently kill good sessions (review-r3 #44)"; commit da00ec9's message confirms the scope: "ENOSPC/IO errors during unzip retry instead of quarantining (#44)". ingest.py:581 `_md5_file(dst / "video.mp4")` reads the entire video with no OSError handling (ingest.py:50-55); run.py:188-197 turns any non-DownloadError exception into `ledger.set_state(sid, "QUARANTINED", f"download crashed: ...")`. The supersede/heal preconditions at ingest.py:207-209, 238, and 272-276 all require a change the uploader never made.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A zip-payload session downloads and extracts cleanly; while _md5_file streams the 8 GB video.mp4 for the dedupe backfill (ingest.py:581), the VM disk returns a transient EIO (or write_script/stub.touch hits ENOSPC while a concurrent batch is still filling the disk above the per-session F7 check). The raw OSError escapes download(), run.py:193 marks the session QUARANTINED, and the alert fires once. On every later scan the Drive folder shows identical bytes/ctime at the same path, so no supersede or heal path re-registers it: a perfectly good player session is permanently dropped from delivery (lost hours for the player and the 1000 h target) even though a retry next run would have succeeded.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In download(), wrap the post-transfer local filesystem work (md5 verify/backfill, sidecar moves, rrd script/stub writes) the same way _unzip_payload does: catch OSError and re-raise as DownloadError(kind="transient") so _download_phase re-queues the session as DISCOVERED; alternatively, in run.py:_download_phase, treat OSError specially (transient re-queue with a retry cap) before the terminal catch-all.
confirmed.verifier_reasoning: Verified. The r3 #44 transient-OSError conversion exists only inside _unzip_payload (ingest.py:471-477, 'host-level errors are TRANSIENT ... review-r3 #44'). Every other filesystem op in download() raises raw OSError: _md5_file (ingest.py:50-55, streams the whole video, called at 535 and 581 — line 581 runs for every zip payload since they arrive with no Drive-side md5), shutil.move of v2 sidecars (565-567), rrdmod.write_script (570), stub.touch (573), dst.mkdir (520/539). run.py:188-195's catch-all turns any non-DownloadError exception into terminal QUARANTINED ('download crashed: ...') — deliberately, per its comment, but that comment's rationale (raw exceptions are never retry-fixable) is exactly what r3 #44 already falsified for host-level OSErrors. No automatic path ever revisits QUARANTINED: the path-heal (ingest.py:207-230) requires a different drive_path, the md5 supersede (238-266) requires a changed md5, the zip supersede (272-294) requires changed bytes or newer ctime — none of which occur for an unchanged good upload; grep confirms no requeue tooling for QUARANTINED anywhere in the package. Mitigating nuance: the quarantine alerts loudly (run.py:196), so it is not silent — but recovery needs manual ledger surgery or a modified re-upload. MAJOR: good sessions permanently stuck/lost to delivery on a transient host error.

Run 2's _recover_split adopts: inserts child rows, unlinks the manifest, and is killed before run.py:379 sets SPLIT. Parent revalidates on its intact work dir; if the verdict now lands bin 1 it goes READY and the WHOLE video is delivered on top of its already-delivered segments (double-delivery of the same footage); if it lands bin 2 with a cut plan, the re-cut overwrites the live children's work dirs mid-flight.

Grep of all parent_id usages shows no guard anywhere preventing the parent from re-verdicting READY/delivering the whole video while its children (INGESTED, riding the batch via _partition_resume's parent mapping, 785-787) validate and deliver segments, nor from re-cutting over the live child dirs on a bin-2 verdict. Kept MAJOR rather than BLOCKER: double-delivery additionally requires the revalidation to flip to bin 1 (possible via VLM nondeterminism, but re-detecting the same defects on the unchanged work dir is the likelier outcome), and the crash window between line 340 and 379 is milliseconds; the likelier consequence is the re-cut clobbering live children — broken-resume/wrong-state class.

confirmed.verifier_reasoning: Verified in ingest.py: any known session id seen at a different drive_path with existing state != QUARANTINED takes the collision branch (231-237) and continues without ever updating drive_path — and the branch never checks whether the OLD path is still present in the current listing, so a Drive-side operator-folder rename (free-text names per the Q5 amendment, acknowledged at ingest.py:129-130, so typo-fix renames are expected) is indistinguishable from a malicious id reuse. download() runs rclone against row['drive_path'] verbatim (525); a nonexistent source fails, and after 3 attempts DownloadError is raised with the default kind='transient' (527-530, class default at 439), which _download_phase routes back to DISCOVERED with a per-run alert (run.py:181-187) — every 30-min tick, forever, with a fresh collision flag per scan. No converging path exists short of manual ledger surgery (the QUARANTINED heal at 209-230 is the only path-update route).
